title: The Unpronounceable Professor explains bech32
description: Many features and development upgrades are first implemented on Litecoin and then later are adopted by Bitcoin. Segwit, Lightning Network transactions and less well known bech32 were all on Litecoin before they were anywhere else. Learn more about what this is and how it works with the The Unpronounceable Professor.

asr.full_text: Welcome to my Litecoin Show. I am Professor Nkutwe Nketwe Nkutwe Nkudakwe and today I want to tell you about how Litecoin indirectly saved you from transferring coins to wrong addresses simply because you mistyped it. It is this simple invention here called the BAC32 format. What you see on the board is a bitcoin address before the back 32 format doesn't look very bitcoin abby now what you see on the board is a bitcoin address after the back 32 format you see how the bc in front helps you recognize it as a bitcoin wallet address that's what back 32 is it is an address format that was introduced together with segwit in order to allow for addresses to be more recognizable. It also made the addresses more compatible with modern systems, more efficient to use and even cheaper. Now, when this was introduced alongside Segwit, the Bitcoin Core aka Bitcoin Developer Circle were very hesitant to implement it. So Litecoin courageously stepped in and implemented this important feature first before Bitcoin followed suit. Yeah, Litecoin has been a pioneer in helping adopt useful technologies so that Bitcoin can adopt them later and even further strengthen itself. And because of this little appreciated role of Litecoin in this space, your chances of transferring coins to the wrong address simply because of a typographical error are significantly reduced. That's it from me today. As usual, I am your Professor Nkutwe Nkwe Nketwe Nmbarakwe and I will see you in the next episode.
